list.sentence: I retrieved forty documents whole and kept twenty-six, leaving out South Asia, the Near East, press relations in Washington, negotiation at the United Nations and internal reporting procedure. ## Decisions this needs from you **What stands for "soft power."** The officials never used the term, so you must choose what counts: a narrower reading (culture and exchange only) drops most of the Vietnam and Thailand material, and a wider one (aid, trade or military posture as image) needs the area volumes' general policy papers, which I did not search for this. **Whether wartime information work belongs.** Keeping counterinsurgency information work in Indochina and Thailand lets Vietnam dominate, since about three in four of the area-volume headings found came from Vietnam volumes; leaving it out keeps the account to persuasion of elites in peacetime. **What "the region" covers.** Leaving out South Asia and the Near East removed nine headings that the word "Asia" matched; taking the Pacific to include Australia and New Zealand adds little, since they appear only in one round-up, as do Korea and Burma. **The .** Accepting the set as it stands leaves those years nearly empty, which may reflect my searches and not the edition; filling them needs a further search of those volumes.
